## Project Description

### Overview

We will build a two-player infrared laser tag system in which each player carries a blaster and a wearable target, both driven by one E155 development board (iCE40 UP5K FPGA + STM32L432KC MCU). Pulling the trigger fires a coded IR packet; when another player's receivers decode it, their unit registers a hit, flashes its LEDs, plays a sound effect, and reports the hit over Wi-Fi to a laptop scoreboard.

### Player Unit

Each player unit contains the following:

- **Blaster:** a 940 nm IR LED behind a focusing lens, driven at a 38 kHz carrier, plus a push-button trigger.
- **Target:** two IR receivers in the baseline (front and back), expandable to six (chest, back, both shoulders) so hits can be scored by body segment.
- **Feedback:** indicator LEDs showing a hit, a speaker for hit as well as win/lose sound effects.
- **Connectivity:** an ESP8266 that streams hit events to a laptop running a polling scoreboard web page.
- **Enclosure:** a 3D-printed housing and straps, powered by a portable battery so players can move freely.

### Relevance to Microprocessors

The project exercises the core course concepts:

- LED display driving (Lab 1)
- Input synchronization (Lab 3)
- Timer-driven audio (Lab 4)
- Interrupts (Lab 5)
- IoT streaming (Lab 6)

The new hardware is the IR transmit/receive chain; the new FPGA content is SPRAM-backed display patterns; the new MCU content is DAC-based audio.
